messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: ectotherm() + DEB: Failure to desiccate?
parts:
Hi Mike,

I can't seem to get a simulated ectotherm to experience any desiccation. I looked up related conversations in the Google Group, and found this one between you and Adam in 2021. Following the steps you suggested there, and doing some other tweaking to simulate what I believe should be an animal that's pretty terrible at holding water, I still see no desiccation (as indicated by PCT_DESIC). Below I provide a toy example, run using the most recent build on GitHub as of today. Can you point me towards how I can get this toy animal to start desiccating?

Thanks,
Dave
library(NicheMapR)
library(ggplot2)

micro <- micro_global(loc = c(145.620, -16.821), PCTWET = 50) #Kuranda, Queensland

ecto <- ectotherm(T_F_min = 30, T_F_max = 35, T_pref = 33, T_B_min = 20,  
                  T_RB_min = 10,
                  DEB = 1, # Turn DEB model on
                  fossorial = 0, aestdepth = 1, # prevent belowground activity
                  pct_H_P = 99, pct_H_N = 99, pct_wet = 100, # maximize water loss
                  pct_H_X = .1,  # minimize water gain
                  raindrink = 1000, # Very high threshold necessary for drinking (mm of rainfall)
                  K_skin = 10, psi_body = -707, H2Obal_init = -1)

# Extract predictions
debout = as.data.frame(ecto$debout)
yearsout = as.data.frame(ecto$yearsout)
yearout = as.data.frame(ecto$yearout)

debout$timestep <- 1:nrow(debout)

# No change to percent desiccation
ggplot(debout) +
  geom_point(aes(timestep, PCT_DESIC))

# No reported desiccation in summary matrices
yearsout$MaxDes
yearout$Pct_Des


--
David Klinges, PhD

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: ectotherm() + DEB: Failure to desiccate?
parts:
Hi Dave,

It's because you ran only 12 days of simulation (because micro_global does the middle day of each month) and it hadn't hatched yet :). Those parameters definitely killed the animal almost immediately after it hatched when I ran the simulation longer. Try this out:

micro <- micro_global(loc = c(145.620, -16.821), nyears = 3, timeinterval = 365) #Kuranda, Queensland

ecto <- ectotherm(T_F_min = 30, T_F_max = 35, T_pref = 33, T_B_min = 20,  
                  T_RB_min = 10,
                  DEB = 1, # Turn DEB model on
                  fossorial = 0, aestdepth = 1, # prevent belowground activity

pct_wet = 0.25, # maximize water loss
                  raindrink = 1000) # Very high threshold necessary for drinking (mm of rainfall)

debout$timestep <- 1:nrow(debout)

# No change to percent desiccation
ggplot(debout) +
  geom_point(aes(timestep, PCT_DESIC))

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: ectotherm() + DEB: Failure to desiccate?
parts:
Hi Mike,

Big thanks! Yep that did it. Admittedly I don't use micro_global much (more micro_era5 and micro_usa plus some local dev versions I have) but should have remembered the timeinterval argument.

And, in exploring here I realized that in my non-toy simulations I had set raindrink to 0 (for others reading this: raindrink sets the threshold amount of rain in mm in order for the animal to rehydrate itself by drinking), so of course the animal wasn't desiccating at all.

Cheers,
Dave
ᐧ
